correctness.rationale: With x₀=0 the edge XOR word determines x uniquely; even parity is necessary and sufficient for closing the ring. A site flips iff both incident edges are 1 and the site is not pinned. XOR of the two endpoint flips with an edge bit shows that a zero never turns on, and that an edge currently 1 turns off exactly when it has just one neighboring 1 in the linear word (virtual zeros at the two ends). Thus both edges of any run of length ≥2 are removed at once, and singleton runs are fixed. This proves that the first fixed time is the largest floor(run length/2), and proves absence of cycles, with the empty-run maximum interpreted as zero. The parity-projected series follows by splitting at zero walls: one capped initial run, then any number of zero-plus-capped-run blocks. The coefficients at n<3 describe formal words; no physical boundary convention there is required. At time floor(n/2) the extremizers are exactly the even all-one word, or the two end-positioned length-(n−1) runs at odd n. The all-zero attractor requires every run length even; these words tile uniquely by 0 and 11, so the Fibonacci recurrence and its initial values follow directly. Division by the 2^(n−1) indexed starts and Binet's identity give the claimed asymptotic. Independent replay /tmp/opencode/frozen_majority_replay.py exhausts lengths 3–16 using bitwise open-string majority, checks each start's time and basin membership, and compares all cumulative counts to a parity/terminal-run-state automaton. At n=8 it gives [27,77,20,3,1] and basin 34; at n=16 [1292,18532,9900,2404,512,104,20,3,1] and basin 1597. The uploaded source and output were inspected without executing them. The unbounded conclusions use run erosion and exact formal-language counting, not the replay.

value.rationale: Worst-case time and fixed-state totals do not answer how often a single immutable opinion wins or how quickly typical starting states freeze. These two natural exact invariants are given uniformly over sizes and times; in particular, certain fixation coexists with exponentially vanishing consensus probability. The value is the two exact pinned invariants, not a new local rule or arbitrary extracted slice.
